assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only 86-eighty-six:grethe-wenzel@original-light-novels#86-grethe-wenzel-character-reference-profile, the canonical CMR-5 Grethe Wenzel character reference profile (version 1.2, release 86-V2-V01-V14-1.0) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the locked original-Japanese light novels, in which she is attested from V02 to V14, with Alter.1 as audited supplemental evidence and Alter.2 excluded. The profile states that its cumulative diagnostic index holds 165 rows (GRE-001 to GRE-165) and that the index, not the prose, is the retrieval surface for Japanese anchors; the profile itself lists only 19 highest-value controls, routed by volume and usually XHTML file but not paragraph. That index is not curated evidence on this subject, and no row, count by volume or anchor is taken from it. The CMR-9 promotion audit and ledger, the profile's validation report, the relationship register matrix, the profile of Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman), the ledgers L01, L02 and L09, Documents 06, 07, 09, 12 and 18, the Phase-5 and Phase-8 artifacts and the Japanese EPUBs are not curated evidence on this subject either, and nothing is borrowed from them. The profile's CMR-9 verdict and its High, Moderate and Open labels are inputs, not conclusions. No anime adaptation, V15+ volume, Alter.2 scene or other character's profile is included, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The profile's located anchors from V02 (the Reginleif design, p-007, and the large-scale offensive, p-008) through V14 (the return to frontline combat, p-008). The profile gives no developmental phase sequence. It distinguishes only an earlier form of protection (children should not be on this battlefield, V03 p-005/006) from a later one (accompaniment, V03 p-007, GRE-159), and it places the burden-ownership formulation in V13 (p-006) and the combat return in V14 (p-008); the V11 grief-and-revenge combat self is retrospective (V11 p-026). Volumes V04-V06, V08-V10 and V12 have no listed control, and the V07 controls have no XHTML file. No default state is set; one of the located anchors must be selected. Alter.1 rows are supplements without volume placement, and states after V14 are not established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The profile gives a causal account of Grethe (Grethe Wenzel): she responds to danger by trying to redesign the conditions under which people must face it, through machines, plans, permissions, staffing or the distribution of responsibility. It says what changes her response: she tolerates danger that belongs to military necessity but moves fastest against danger made worse by avoidable structure (wrong safety assumptions, a unit selected because nobody will complain if it dies, responsibility pushed downward, a subordinate discounting self-preservation), so she is a preventable-risk and unfair-burden minimizer rather than a blanket risk minimizer (V03 p-005/006, GRE-016 to GRE-022). Her decision habit is alternatives before refusal, distinguishing grounds to object from jurisdiction to cancel (the Nachtzehrer solution, V03 p-007). It predicts her mistakes: technical correctness that is not humane fit (the Reginleif's human-factors danger, V02 p-007); engineering a troubling mission into feasibility; grief that blurs protecting people with destroying what hurt them (V03 Morpho exchange; V11 p-026, GRE-116); and treating military competence as political competence (V11 p-026, GRE-106, V11-L036). A would overclaim: the set is one derived artifact whose listed controls are routed only to file or 'vicinity', its 165-row index is outside the set, the profile rates the balance of grief projection and conviction and the persistence of her combat identity as moderate, and the post-V14 outcome is open. C would understate an account that says which consideration decides between objecting, redesigning, accepting risk and joining it, and predicts her characteristic errors.

The profile records one developmental correction for Grethe (Grethe Wenzel): the early impulse that children should not be on this battlefield (V03 p-005/006) becomes accompaniment, changing the conditions around their choice rather than choosing their identity (V03 p-007, GRE-159). It adds located later anchors (the V11 retreat and the retrospective grief-and-revenge self remembered by Richard (Richard Altner), V11 p-026; the V13 burden-ownership formulation, p-006, GRE-160 and GRE-161; the V14 return to frontline combat after roughly a decade, p-008, GRE-162) and says her attention to burden distribution grows over time. B would overclaim: the profile has no developmental trajectory section and no phase sequence; 'early' and 'later' are not placed by volume beyond V03; V04-V06, V08-V10 and V12 have no listed control; and how her combat identity persists after the V14 emergency is only moderate. D would understate a located correction with a stated mechanism and located later anchors.

The profile fixes the written-Japanese register of Grethe (Grethe Wenzel): first person 私, rendered わたし at heightened protective moments (V14 p-008); an adult feminine professional-casual baseline with junior officers and familiar colleagues (～よ, ～わ, ～のよ, ～かしら, ～なさい, ～頂戴) and rank address (エマ中尉, V14 p-008, GRE-163); disciplined upward formality that stays recognizable under moral anger (質問をよろしいでしょうか。少将); familiar combat roughness blending rough lexis with feminine endings (なめるんじゃないわよ、ガキ, V03 p-007, GRE-028); targeted anger (わたしの可愛い部下たちを、よくも、傷つけてくれた, V14 p-008, GRE-162, V14-L157); command ownership (あなたたちは手足で、頭は私。銃爪の責任は私にあるわ, V13 p-006); and denser, faster technical vocabulary when excited (Alter.1 part0062, GRE-165). It states that humor does not collapse her register and that she is neither hyper-soft nor masculine. C would understate located morphology, verbatim exemplars by state and recipient class and explicit negative constraints. A is rejected: there is no frequency data, the upward-formality exemplar has no location, personal address toward Shin (Shinei Nouzen), Lena (Vladilena Milizé), Richard (Richard Altner), Willem (Willem Ehrenfried) and Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) is not given beyond rank address and ガキ under combat, and the L09 voice ledger is outside the set.

The profile says ordinary life for Grethe (Grethe Wenzel) is part of what military effort preserves, and that her sentiment becomes logistics: helping turn birthdays for thousands of Eighty-Six into monthly celebrations (Alter.1, GRE-153), giving Lena (Vladilena Milizé) a wine-red lipstick (Alter.1, GRE-155), and technical hobby enthusiasm with Willem (Willem Ehrenfried) when nothing depends on it (Alter.1 part0062, GRE-165), with participation in parties, travel, manners instruction (V07, GRE-076), bars and games as one adult among many. B would overclaim: the located ordinary rows are few and mostly Alter.1 without volume placement or paragraph, the parties, bars and travel have no listed control, and there is no routine. D would understate stated drivers with located controls and a prediction (technical specificity and logistics in ordinary settings).

The profile distinguishes directed relations of Grethe (Grethe Wenzel) and says how her conduct changes by relation class: upward, disciplined formality, reasoned challenge and alternative plans that become visible anger when disposability hides inside necessity (V03 p-005/006); downward, direct correction translated into the listener's own values (telling Shin (Shinei Nouzen) that protecting himself protects others, V02 p-008) and praise of action under fear rather than fearlessness (Anju (Anju Emma), V14 p-008, GRE-163); with old peers, sharper teasing and biographical shorthand. Partner rows: Shin as engineer and user, commander and subordinate, adult and teenager, with roughness under combat (V03 p-007, GRE-028) and the accompaniment correction (GRE-159); Lena (Vladilena Milizé) as a junior whose political judgment may exceed hers (V11 p-026, GRE-106); the Eighty-Six as 'my' soldiers without ownership (V14 p-008); Richard (Richard Altner) as superior, old comrade and memory witness (V03; V11 p-026, GRE-116, GRE-164); and Willem (Willem Ehrenfried) as a prickly old friend (V07, GRE-076; Alter.1, GRE-165). C would understate class-level discrimination tied to located partner rows. A is rejected: the relation with Annette (Annette Penrose) has no listed control, the profile says its strongest evidence on Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) is routed through Ernst's own profile, which is outside the set, the long-term forms of her adult relations are open, and the matrix and L02 are outside the set.

Private states of Grethe (Grethe Wenzel) are located at a few points: narration that she keeps her lipstick on after her face loses color so subordinates will not read her fear (V02 p-008, GRE-010); the Nachtzehrer flight, where narration compares her sharper laughter to an adrenaline high and the return of an old battlefield feeling (V03 p-007); her partial acceptance of the grief projection Richard (Richard Altner) names (V03 p-005/006); and the protective combat thought in V14 (p-008). These tie to choices: contained command, self-selection as pilot, continued protection despite mixed motive, and re-entry into combat. B would overclaim: most states are inferred from expression and conduct, the V11 grief-and-revenge self is reported through Richard's memory rather than her interior, the located rows are not classified by focalization, and no paragraph is given. D would understate narrated interior states causally tied to her conduct.

The profile states the conflict sequence of Grethe (Grethe Wenzel) with superiors: begin inside professional form, ask leave to question, present capability arguments and alternatives, and let the temperature rise sharply when disposability hides inside necessity, without confusing grounds to object with jurisdiction to cancel (the Morpho mission, V03 p-005/006). With subordinates she corrects directly with a practical rationale (V02 p-008); with old peers she argues with more irritation and banter (V07, GRE-076; Alter.1, GRE-165); when she cannot win she looks for the next technical, logistical or procedural lever (the Nachtzehrer, V03 p-007). C would understate conditioned response families with located examples. A is rejected: the Morpho mission is the one fully described conflict with a superior, the V11 grief-driven combat self is retrospective, conflict in which grief is active now is unsampled, and anchors are file-level.

The profile gives Grethe (Grethe Wenzel) located positions and a failure mode: preventing needless child death is legitimate even when her motive is partly grief (V03 p-005/006, GRE-020 to GRE-022); the Eighty-Six's choices are not hers to erase, but command owes them conditions in which choice is not disposability (V03 p-007, GRE-159); lethal force is avoided as long as possible and, if necessary, she orders it and owns the responsibility rather than letting junior officers carry it (ぎりぎりまで、そうしなくて済むようにするわ。でも、必要ならそれを命じる; V13 p-006, GRE-160, GRE-161); and competence is compatible with fear (V14 p-008, GRE-163). It predicts the error of making a morally troubling mission executable by solving its technical problem, and it bounds the V13 'hands and head' language as burden ownership, not a doctrine erasing subordinate conscience. C would understate located positions with a reasoning pattern and failure mode. A is rejected: the V13 formulation is a stated intention in one scene rather than an observed order, political judgment is an explicit weakness, and no postwar choice is modeled.

The profile gives four comic modes for Grethe (Grethe Wenzel): dry senior-officer teasing about promotions, pay and social situations; mischief through institutional access (the mission-recorder prank); disproportionate technical enthusiasm (Alter.1 part0062, GRE-165); and combat gallows energy (なめるんじゃないわよ、ガキ, V03 p-007, GRE-028). It states that humor becomes sparse when she carries command responsibility for mass casualties or lethal force against civilians, and that she can be embarrassed in Alter.1. B would overclaim: dry teasing and embarrassment have no listed control, the prose places the mission-recorder prank in V04 while the scene bank lists the mission-recorder control (GRE-072) under V07 without a file, and two of four modes rest on one row each. D would understate stated modes with a suspension condition and two located forms.

The curated item is a dedicated canonical profile of Grethe (Grethe Wenzel) over V02-V14 with Alter.1, but within it the evidence routing is thin: it names 19 highest-value controls, routed to volume and usually XHTML file, several only as a 'vicinity' of an index ID, the V07 controls without a file, and none to paragraph. It states that its 165-row index is the retrieval surface and that the prose should not replace the indexed Japanese anchors, and that index is not curated on this row. V04-V06, V08-V10 and V12 have no listed control. C would overclaim: the profile itself defers anchor-level support to an uncurated index, and most volumes are unrepresented in what the set contains. E would understate a dedicated profile with verbatim Japanese exemplars and file-level routes for key controls in V02, V03, V07, V11, V13, V14 and Alter.1.

For Grethe (Grethe Wenzel) there are seven counterexamples with results, twelve mischaracterization traps and eighteen would-sound-wrong constraints. The counterexamples reject 'always prioritizes safety' (the Reginleif, the Nachtzehrer and the V14 combat return), 'never instrumental' (the V13 'hands and head' language, read narrowly), 'pure altruism' (the accepted grief projection), 'natural politician' (V11 p-026, GRE-106, V11-L036), 'rear-echelon intellectual', 'maternal toward everyone younger' and 'accepting a mission means believing it clean'. C would understate these affirmative constraints, several of them located. A is rejected: most traps and constraints are profile rules without a listed control, the located ones are file-level, and limits after V14 are open.

Controls for Grethe (Grethe Wenzel) are placed by volume and usually XHTML file: V02 p-007 and p-008, V03 p-005/006, p-007 and p-009, V11 p-026, V13 p-006 and p-007, V14 p-008 and Alter.1 part0062. C would overclaim: no row is placed to a paragraph, the V07 controls have no file, several controls are a 'vicinity' of an index ID, no volume is split at a located state change, the profile gives no phase sequence or default state, and V04-V06, V08-V10 and V12 have no listed control. E would understate volume and file placement for each listed control and the separation of the V03 correction, the V11 retrospective, V13 and V14.

conditions: Illustrative textual Japanese only, never quotation, with 私 as first person (わたし only at heightened protective moments) and the adult feminine professional-casual baseline (～よ, ～わ, ～のよ, ～かしら, ～なさい, ～頂戴) with juniors and familiar colleagues; never coy, childlike, maternal-soft or masculine as a baseline.

Upward speech is disciplined and rank-aware and may carry low, targeted anger without losing syntax; rank address with surname (as エマ中尉) is used where military role matters; ガキ appears only in familiar combat challenge toward Shin (Shinei Nouzen). No personal address toward Lena (Vladilena Milizé), Richard (Richard Altner), Willem (Willem Ehrenfried) or Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) is invented.
Technical talk becomes more specific and faster, not merely enthusiastic; humor stays adult; command-level lethal decisions are owned in her own voice.
No frequency distribution, anime performance or state after V14 is claimed; output that depends on one abstains.
scenario_readiness.note: Located morphology and verbatim exemplars by state and recipient class constrain illustrative output. Missing personal address and frequency data restrict recipients and form rather than blocking use.

conditions: Chronology is one explicitly selected located anchor; there is no default: V02 Reginleif and offensive command; V03 Morpho objection, before the accompaniment correction; V03 Nachtzehrer and after the correction (p-007, GRE-159); V11 brigade retreat; V13 command at the lethal-order decision (p-006); or V14 frontline return (p-008). V04-V10 and V12 are excluded as chronology, nothing after V14 is used, and Alter.1 rows do not fix a state.

The interlocutor is a sampled relation in its attested class: a superior officer in briefing or argument, Shin (Shinei Nouzen), Lena (Vladilena Milizé), Anju (Anju Emma) or the Eighty-Six as her subordinates, Richard (Richard Altner) or Willem (Willem Ehrenfried). Annette (Annette Penrose) and Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) are excluded. Transfer to another junior officer is a separate, lower-confidence condition justified by the downward class pattern.

The situation matches a sampled class: a mission whose selection logic may make soldiers disposable, a technical or logistical problem that alters survivability, a lethal-force decision she controls as commander, subordinates harmed, a subordinate discounting self-preservation, or ordinary celebration, gift-giving and technical banter.

Output predicts her characteristic errors (technically correct but humanly unfit solutions, engineering a troubling mission into feasibility, grief blurring protection and destruction, overreach into political judgment) and never makes her a pacifist, a pure technocrat or a political strategist.

It abstains on a present-tense grief crisis beyond the V14 protective re-entry, her postwar role, the long-term forms of her adult relations and any romantic conclusion; it introduces no institution, technology or relationship state absent from V02-V14.

Annette (Annette Penrose) and Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman) are excluded. Another junior officer is a separate, lower-confidence transfer.
setting_constraints: Federacy and allied military briefing rooms, laboratories and hangars, cockpits, command posts and battlefields within V02-V14, or Alter.1 celebrations and leisure without volume placement
No political governance role, postwar career, Alter.2 or V15+ setting

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded to located anchors, sampled relation classes and situation classes. Unlocated volumes, unsampled relations, political governance and grief-driven crisis states are excluded rather than inferred.

conditions: Sampled ordinary classes only: organizing celebrations (birthdays as a logistics problem), choosing gifts that carry presentation and agency, technical hobby argument with Willem (Willem Ehrenfried), and participation in group social life as one adult among many.
Sentiment tends to become logistics and technical talk becomes specific; she can be teased, embarrassed and annoyed without dropping her adult register.
No invented routine, tastes, domestic life or hobbies beyond those attested.
scenario_readiness.note: A few located Alter.1 controls with stated drivers support narrow extrapolation. The sparse, unplaced sample blocks broader use.

conditions: Situation classes the profile samples: a unit selected because its deaths would not be contested, protection with an acknowledged grief motive, a risky choice by young soldiers she can accompany but not erase, and command authorization of lethal force.

Reasoning distinguishes necessary from preventable risk and grounds to object from jurisdiction to cancel, offers alternatives before refusal, and keeps naming the compromise after a technical solution makes a mission feasible.
The selected anchor matters: before the V03 correction she may argue for withdrawing young soldiers from battle; after it she argues for accompaniment.
No political or governance judgment, and no lethal order beyond the V13 class in which she controls the conditions.
scenario_readiness.note: Located positions with a reasoning pattern, a correction and a predicted failure mode support bounded ethical extrapolation within the sampled classes.

The profile affirmatively leaves romance for Grethe (Grethe Wenzel) unestablished: it notes only old romantic or biographical jokes around Willem (Willem Ehrenfried) in Alter.1 and lists any romantic conclusion within the locked boundary as open. CONDITIONAL would require inventing a relationship state the profile does not establish.

conditions: The selected anchor fixes the role: Reginleif engineer and field-grade commander (V02 p-007/p-008), objecting officer and Nachtzehrer pilot (V03 p-005/006, p-007), brigade commander in retreat (V11 p-026), commander owning a lethal-order decision (V13 p-006), or frontline combatant after years away (V14 p-008).

Attention runs to capability, failure points and who carries the burden; fear is contained in presentation while function continues; she argues upward through procedure and alternatives and takes risk herself when she holds a needed skill.
Political-symbolic judgment is outside her strength and is deferred; no postwar professional role is modeled.
scenario_readiness.note: Her most densely evidenced domain. Located roles with stated decision patterns and an explicit domain limit support bounded extrapolation within one selected anchor; file-level routing limits confidence.

known_limits.statement: The source boundary is locked original-Japanese V02-V14 for Grethe (Grethe Wenzel), with Alter.1 supplemental and Alter.2 excluded. The final-arc outcome, her postwar role, whether her frontline combat identity persists after the V14 emergency and the long-term forms of her relations with Ernst (Ernst Zimmerman), Willem (Willem Ehrenfried) and other adult peers are Moderate or Open in the profile.
